reason: S1 creates the independently public, stateful wuffs_adler32__hasher API, but H0 only invokes wuffs_adler32__hasher__update indirectly through wuffs_zlib__decoder__decode. That route supplies only bytes produced by wuffs_deflate__decoder__decode and cannot directly control arbitrary slice contents, lengths, or update-call partitioning. This is a material gap for the newly exposed Adler-32 entry point and was introduced by moving the former private wuffs_zlib__adler32 implementation into public std/adler32 APIs.
evidence: S0 defines wuffs_zlib__adler32 and wuffs_zlib__adler32__update as private zlib implementation details; S1 removes them.
S1 adds public wuffs_adler32__hasher, wuffs_adler32__hasher__initialize, and wuffs_adler32__hasher__update in gen/c/std/adler32.c and std/adler32/common_adler32.wuffs.
H0 initializes only wuffs_zlib__decoder and calls only wuffs_zlib__decoder__set_ignore_checksum and wuffs_zlib__decoder__decode.

Within wuffs_zlib__decoder__decode, wuffs_adler32__hasher__update receives a slice from a_dst.private_impl.mark to b_wptr_dst, so its input and call boundaries are mediated by zlib/deflate decoding rather than directly fuzz-controlled.
wuffs_adler32__hasher__update preserves f_state across calls, making arbitrary segmentation and repeated-update sequences part of the newly public stateful API surface.
recommended_action: Add a dedicated Adler-32 harness that initializes wuffs_adler32__hasher, feeds arbitrary fuzz bytes directly to wuffs_adler32__hasher__update, and fuzz-controls segmentation across repeated update calls.
